evaluated.name: Equity-Financed Intangible Expansion
evaluated.hypothesis: Balance-sheet intangibles that expand precisely when the firm is issuing equity indicate stock-financed acquisition of soft assets at inflated valuations rather than organically created intangible capital.
evaluated.reasoning: Managers issue overvalued equity and deploy it into acquired intangibles and goodwill, so the joint occurrence of issuance and intangible growth is a sharper overvaluation marker than either component alone. The multiplicative rank form fires only when both conditions hold, capturing the conditional market-timing mechanism instead of the additive average of two weak effects.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Debt-Financed Acquired Intangibles
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(dltis, dltr), at)), RANK(RATIO(DELTA(COALESCE(gdwl, intan), 1), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Net long-term debt raised to buy goodwill and acquired intangibles creates leveraged claims backed by non-collateralizable soft assets, which subsequently underperform through impairment risk and debt overhang on future innovation.
evaluated.reasoning: Goodwill additions financed with new long-term debt combine two fragilities: an unverifiable asset and a hard fixed claim, so integration failure triggers write-offs while the debt service crowds out productive spending. Using goodwill where reported and total intangibles otherwise keeps the acquired-intangible interpretation without a blanket coverage patch.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Productivity-Signed Intangible Financing
evaluated.expression: MUL(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), at), SIGN(TREND(RATIO(revt, MA(xrd, 3)), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The same net external financing is good news when the firm's realized R&D productivity (revenue generated per dollar of smoothed R&D) is improving and bad news when it is deteriorating; the sign of the innovation payoff trend switches the interpretation of the financing flow.
evaluated.reasoning: This directly implements the task's distinction: financing raised by firms whose intangible investment is demonstrably converting into sales funds positive-NPV innovation, while financing raised amid falling R&D productivity is opportunistic issuance into a deteriorating franchise. Multiplying the financing intensity by the sign of a five-year productivity trend makes the interaction genuinely conditional and sign-flipping rather than a monotone blend of two signals.

evaluated.name: Payout-Signed R&D Intensity
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(xrd, at), 3), 2)), NEG(SIGN(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dvc)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The pricing of R&D intensity is conditional on how it is funded: peer-adjusted R&D carries the intangible-value premium only for firms that are simultaneously net returners of capital (repurchases plus dividends exceeding equity and debt issued), while the same R&D intensity funded by net external issuance signals capital-market-dependent, market-timed spending and should predict low returns.
evaluated.reasoning: Instead of adding two anomaly ranks, the financing theme enters only as a sign switch that flips the sign of the intangible signal, so high-R&D externally financed firms are placed in the short leg rather than merely being ranked lower. Low-R&D firms sit near zero regardless of financing, which means the long-short spread is identified purely by the funding-source contrast within intangible-intensive firms, not by either standalone effect.

evaluated.name: Issuance Timed Away From Innovation
evaluated.hypothesis: Equity issued in a year when the firm's own R&D intensity is at a five-year low is not financing innovation; it is opportunistic capital raised while the intangible investment program is idle, which is the clearest expression of overvaluation-driven issuance.
evaluated.reasoning: TS_RANK normalizes R&D against the firm's own history, so the signal is not a cross-sectional R&D-intensity anomaly in disguise; it measures within-firm timing mismatch between the financing event and the innovation cycle. The multiplicative form activates only when large issuance coincides with an innovation lull, distinguishing genuine R&D funding rounds (which should be neutral or good) from paper-selling.

evaluated.name: Financing Surplus Over Intangible Needs
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), at), RATIO(ADD(xrd, DELTA(intan, 1)), at)), 5)), INDICATOR(RATIO(ADD(xrd, intan), at), 0.05))
evaluated.hypothesis: Among intangible-intensive firms, external capital raised well in excess of contemporaneous intangible investment (R&D expense plus the increase in the intangible balance) represents financing without a matching innovation use, i.e., valuation-driven issuance; conversely, intangible spending exceeding external funds raised is self-financed innovation.
evaluated.reasoning: Both legs are scaled by total assets rather than by a near-zero intangible base, so the measure is a bounded financing-need gap rather than an inverse-intangible-intensity artifact, and 5% symmetric winsorization removes the residual tail influence the critic flagged. The indicator restricts active values to firms with a meaningful intangible base (above 5% of assets), placing non-intangible firms at a neutral zero so that both portfolio legs are drawn from the population where the mechanism actually applies.

evaluated.name: Debt-Funded Innovation Discount
evaluated.hypothesis: Debt is the wrong contract for non-collateralizable innovation: R&D-intensive firms funding with net new long-term debt face debt overhang and distress-driven cuts to the research program, so their intangible investment is not rewarded and is instead penalized.
evaluated.reasoning: This is deliberately the instrument-isolating twin of Signal 1 — identical intangible leg, identical scaling, only the financing instrument changes — so the pair identifies whether the gen-0 externally-financed-R&D premium comes from equity (state-contingent, upside-sharing) or from debt (fixed claims on soft assets). Gen-0's Debt-Financed Acquired Intangibles already showed a strongly negative FMB slope for the debt-plus-intangibles combination, which this cleanly re-tests on organic rather than acquired intangibles.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Levered Soft-Asset Balance Sheet
evaluated.hypothesis: The interaction that matters may be a stock-level mismatch rather than a flow event: firms whose asset base is dominated by intangibles yet carry high leverage have financed soft, low-liquidation-value assets with hard claims, leaving them exposed to impairment and refinancing shocks that investors underweight.
evaluated.reasoning: All gen-0 proposals used financing *flows*, and the flow measures forced coverage down to 4-10% of firm-months; both intan and total debt are broadly reported, so this tests the same economic tension at much higher coverage and on a persistent state variable with slower portfolio turnover. It is a distinct channel from Signals 1-2 because no issuance event is required — the mispricing is in the standing capital-structure/asset-composition mismatch.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Innovation Under Unstable External Funding
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(xrd, at), 3), 2)), ZSCORE(RANK(VOL(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), at), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: What distinguishes productive from opportunistic intangible financing may be the *stability* of the funding channel: research programs supported by a smooth, repeatable financing pattern are credible, while research funded by erratic, opportunistic capital-market raids is fragile and prone to abandonment.
evaluated.reasoning: This is a second-moment mechanism absent from the archive — it conditions the intangible signal on financing volatility rather than financing level or direction, so it can separate the level effect found in Signal 1 from a fragility effect. If Signal 1 is positive and this is negative, the joint reading is that external funding of R&D is priced as risk only when the funding channel is reliable.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Proceeds-Into-Research Issuance
evaluated.hypothesis: Equity raised while the firm's own research effort is at a five-year high is capital whose use of proceeds is visibly the research program; such firms are financing-dependent innovators whose exposure to funding risk is compensated, whereas firms retiring stock at the peak of their own research cycle are harvesting rather than investing.
evaluated.reasoning: The intangible leg is now a non-negative within-firm state in [0,1] rather than a demeaned cross-sectional score, so firms in a research lull collapse toward a neutral zero and the symmetric "low-R&D/low-issuance also scores high" artifact the critic identified is removed. Because the expected sign is opposite to the standard net-equity-issuance anomaly, a positive result cannot be a relabelling of that anomaly — it specifically requires that issuance is not punished when it coincides with a firm-history peak in research intensity, which is exactly the productive-versus-opportunistic distinction the task poses.

evaluated.name: Paper-For-Intangibles Versus Cash-For-Shares
evaluated.expression: WINSOR(SUB(MIN(RATIO(sstk, at), MUL(RATIO(DELTA(intan, 1), at), INDICATOR(DELTA(intan, 1), 0))), MIN(RATIO(prstkc, at), MUL(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(intan, 1), at)), INDICATOR(NEG(DELTA(intan, 1)), 0)))), 2)
evaluated.hypothesis: The overvaluation signature is equity issued and intangible assets simultaneously built up (paper exchanged for soft assets), while the mirror case — cash returned to shareholders as the intangible base is written down or divested — reflects disciplined redeployment; the return spread should run from the first group to the second.
evaluated.reasoning: The indicator gates make each MIN a conjunction of two strictly non-negative, identically asset-scaled dollar flows, so the previous defect — a bottom leg populated by intangible impairments rather than by the absence of stock-financed expansion — is eliminated. Subtracting the symmetric repurchase-with-intangible-contraction term gives the signal a populated, economically meaningful negative tail instead of a large tie block at zero, which should improve the reliability of the long-short alpha rather than only the cross-sectional slope.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Issuance Into the Unrecorded-Intangible Gap
evaluated.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), at), 2), RANK(SUB(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(xrd, 3), at)), RANK(RATIO(intan, at)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Valuation opacity is greatest where economic intangible capital is large but almost none of it appears on the balance sheet; net equity raised by firms sitting in that expensed-knowledge gap is the hardest for investors to monitor and is where proceeds are most likely to reflect timing rather than verified projects.
evaluated.reasoning: The financing leg is now a split-immune dollar flow, net share issuance scaled by assets, rather than csho growth, so stock splits and stock dividends can no longer dominate the extreme decile. The conditioning weight is not intangible intensity itself but the *gap* between three-year accumulated R&D and recorded intangibles, so the signal is switched off for transparent firms and for firms whose intangibles are already capitalized, making the effect an identified opacity interaction rather than a monotone restatement of the issuance anomaly.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Issuance Into Decaying Research Productivity
evaluated.hypothesis: Productive intangible financing should occur when each research dollar is converting into more revenue; net equity raised while revenue per unit of smoothed R&D is on a downward trend is capital raised into a deteriorating innovation franchise and should predict poor returns.
evaluated.reasoning: This repairs gen-0's Productivity-Signed Intangible Financing, whose SIGN switch threw away trend magnitude and whose two-sided structure produced a near-zero alpha (-0.5%, t -0.65); here the productivity trend enters as a bounded, magnitude-preserving rank weight that switches the signal off for firms with improving research productivity. It tests whether the issuance penalty is driven by observable innovation-output decay rather than by the level or timing of research spending.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Issuance by Goodwill-Built Firms
evaluated.hypothesis: The penalty to equity issuance should be concentrated in firms whose intangible base was purchased rather than created: goodwill-heavy balance sheets combine a history of paying premia with an asset that cannot be verified or liquidated, so new equity raised there is the least monitorable.
evaluated.reasoning: Paired against Signal 1, this asks whether the issuance-intangible interaction lives in *acquired* or *organic* intangible capital — a first-order economic question the archive has not separated, since gen-0's debt-plus-goodwill test mixed instruments and used the failed rank-product form. Treating unreported goodwill as zero is the economically correct convention (no reported goodwill means no acquired intangibles) and lifts coverage well above the R&D-reporter-only signals.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Intangible Contraction After the Raise
evaluated.hypothesis: The revelation phase of overvaluation-driven intangible financing is a shrinking intangible base after a multi-year equity raise: proceeds were capitalized into intangibles that are now being written down or divested, and investors underreact to this confirmation that the funded projects failed.
evaluated.reasoning: This is a lead-lag mechanism absent from the archive — all prior signals pair *contemporaneous* financing and intangible flows, whereas this pairs an accumulated past raise with current intangible contraction, so it identifies failure revelation rather than the raise itself. The bounded contraction rank leaves expanding-intangible issuers near zero, so the short leg is populated only by firms in which both the financing history and the intangible unwind are present.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Abnormal Issuance During an Abnormal Research Ramp
evaluated.expression: MUL(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), at), MA(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), at), 3)), 2), RANK(SUB(RATIO(xrd, at), MA(RATIO(xrd, at), 3))))
evaluated.hypothesis: What identifies story-driven financing is not that a firm issues equity, but that it issues *unusually much for itself* in the very year its research spending is *unusually high for itself*; that synchronization is the signature of a raise marketed on an innovation narrative, and it should be followed by weak returns.
evaluated.reasoning: Both legs are demeaned against the firm's own three-year average, so chronic issuers and chronic non-issuers sit near zero and the cross-sectional composite-issuance anomaly the critic identified is differenced out — what remains is purely the within-firm timing coincidence of the funding event and the research ramp. The R&D deviation enters as a bounded [0,1] weight rather than a second signed term, so firms whose research is at or below their own norm are neutralized instead of generating an unintended symmetric prediction.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Dividend Commitment at Knowledge-Intensive Firms
evaluated.hypothesis: A recurring cash dividend is a hard-to-fake commitment that the firm's expensed knowledge capital generates durable cash flow; that signal carries information only where assets are unverifiable, so among research-intensive firms dividend commitment should identify undervalued intangible capital, while research-intensive firms that pay nothing and lean on markets are the weak end.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the gross-margin proxy the critic correctly called a non-intangible stand-in with an explicit, sale-scaled R&D intensity, and it swaps the repurchase leg — which is the published net-issuance anomaly in mirror form — for the dividend channel, whose standalone cross-sectional return predictability is far weaker, so the spread must come from the interaction rather than from two known main effects. The intangible leg is a non-negative [0,1] gate, so commodity firms' dividends are switched off and the long-short legs are drawn only from firms where verification is genuinely hard.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Financing Accelerating as Intangible Investment Decelerates
evaluated.expression: MUL(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), at), 1), 2), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(xrd, DELTA(intan, 1)), at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The clean market-timing case is divergence in changes: a firm that steps up its external capital raising in the same year that it steps *down* its intangible investment is raising money that demonstrably is not going into innovation, whereas a joint step-up in both is genuine project funding.
evaluated.reasoning: The gen-0 signal compared financing and intangible spending in levels, which mostly ranks firms by their standing business model; this compares their year-over-year *changes*, so the same firm is its own benchmark and the signal fires on a genuine divergence event rather than on a static financing-to-intangible ratio. The deceleration term enters as a bounded rank weight so that firms increasing intangible investment are gated toward zero, preserving the conditional cross-theme element the critic noted was lost when the indicator gate was dropped.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Payout Accelerating as Research Decelerates
evaluated.hypothesis: The harvesting decision is observable as an event: distributions stepping up in the same year that research intensity steps down is an explicit reallocation of cash away from the innovation program and toward shareholders, and it should mark the beginning of franchise decline.
evaluated.reasoning: This isolates level versus change within the payout-harvesting channel — Signal 2 asks whether *high* distributions at *research-intensive* firms are bad, while this asks whether *rising* distributions alongside *falling* research are bad — and the change-based architecture is the one that already worked in gen-2 (alpha -1.9%, t -2.22). Together the pair tells us whether the harvesting effect is a slow-moving state characteristic or a datable reallocation event, which determines how the direction should be refined later.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Issuance While Losing the Innovation Race
evaluated.hypothesis: What matters for the value of intangible financing is the firm's research position relative to its competitors, not its absolute spending: a firm raising equity while its R&D intensity slips down the industry ranking is funding a losing position in an innovation race, and the market is slow to recognize competitive displacement.
evaluated.reasoning: Every intangible conditioner in the archive is firm-specific (own level, own trend, own history), so competitive position is a genuinely new economic channel and its weight — the one-year change in a firm's within-industry R&D-intensity rank — is continuous, bounded, and free of the tied masses that broke earlier sorts. It should also be cleaner than raw productivity trends because industry ranking automatically nets out sector-wide research cycles and technology-cost shocks that contaminate sale-per-R&D.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: External Funding Intensity of the Research Program
evaluated.hypothesis: The economically meaningful quantity is how many dollars of outside capital the firm takes in per dollar it spends on research: a research program financed largely from outside funds is exposed to funding withdrawal and is the natural home of story-driven issuance, whereas a program covered by internal resources is self-validating.
evaluated.reasoning: This abandons the product architecture entirely and normalizes the financing flow by the intangible flow itself, so the interaction is in the units of the measure rather than in a multiplicative weight — it is not the instrument ablation the critic objected to. The denominator is a three-year average of R&D restricted to reporters (never near zero), the ratio is winsorized at 5% tails, and industry ranking makes the final score bounded and comparable across sectors with very different normal funding-to-research ratios, which addresses the blow-up defect of the gen-0 attempt at a ratio form.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Shareholder Cash Versus Research Dollars
evaluated.hypothesis: Within a firm's internal capital allocation, the split between cash sent to shareholders and cash spent on research reveals management's own assessment of the remaining project set; a rising ratio of distributions to research means the intangible pipeline is being wound down, and the market underweights that internal signal.
evaluated.reasoning:
Scaling payout by research rather than by assets or market value breaks the identification with payout yield: a high-payout firm that also funds research heavily scores mid-range, while a modest payer that has cut research to the bone scores at the top, so the sort is on allocation composition rather than on the known payout/net-financing anomalies. It states the harvesting mechanism as a directly measurable allocation choice rather than borrowing the realized sign of a prior product-form signal.

evaluated.hypothesis: The productive pole of intangible financing is a firm expanding its research effort in a year when it is a net *returner* of capital to markets: the expansion is being paid for out of internally generated funds, which is a costly, non-imitable confirmation that the projects are worth funding.
evaluated.reasoning: The financing variable now enters only as a participation gate, never as a magnitude, so the signal cannot be a rescaling of the net-debt-issuance anomaly the critic identified — the ranked quantity is the change in research intensity, and only its measurement is conditioned on self-funding. Because gated firms' R&D growth spans both signs, the long and short legs are both populated by self-funded firms while non-qualifying firms sit at a neutral zero in the middle, which is the opposite of the degenerate-bottom-leg configuration that broke earlier gated signals.

evaluated.name: Debt Share of New Funds at Research-Intensive Firms
evaluated.expression: MUL(MUL(RANK(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(xrd, sale), 3), 2)), ZSCORE(RANK(RATIO(dltis, ADD(dltis, sstk))))), INDICATOR(RATIO(ADD(dltis, sstk), at), 0.02))
evaluated.hypothesis: Conditional on actually raising capital, the instrument mix matters for firms whose assets are research-based: taking the marginal dollar as debt rather than equity places fixed claims against non-collateralizable knowledge assets and makes the research program hostage to refinancing and covenant pressure.

The indicator restricts the signal to firms that raised at least 2% of assets, so the mix is measured only where it is economically meaningful and non-raisers are parked at a neutral zero rather than contaminating either extreme leg.

evaluated.expression: IND_RANK(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(ADD(dvc, prstkc), MA(xrd, 3)), MA(RATIO(ADD(dvc, prstkc), MA(xrd, 3)), 3)), 5))
evaluated.hypothesis: Harvesting is a change in internal capital allocation, not a permanent firm type: the informative event is a firm moving *above its own recent norm* in dollars sent to shareholders per dollar spent on research, which reveals a newly emptied project set rather than an established mature business model.

Subtracting the firm's own three-year average of the same allocation ratio strips out the permanent maturity component while preserving the harvesting mechanism, so this is the decisive test of whether any of that large alpha is attributable to the economic event rather than to firm type.

evaluated.name: Issuance as Pricing Power Erodes
evaluated.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), at), 2), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Gross margin is the realized output of brand, customer and organizational capital; equity raised in a year when that margin is compressing is capital raised as the intangible franchise is being competed away, which is the observable, high-coverage counterpart of raising money into a decaying research franchise.

Margin change is continuous with no tied mass, avoiding the degenerate-weight failure that broke the goodwill and intangible-contraction sorts.

evaluated.name: New Claims Per Dollar of Total Intangible Capital
evaluated.expression: IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), ADD(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3), intan)), 5))
evaluated.hypothesis: What existing shareholders should fear is new outside claims issued against a given stock of intangible capital; measuring financing against the *total* intangible base — accumulated research spending plus capitalized intangibles — rather than against the current research flow captures dilution of the knowledge and brand capital that current owners already hold.

evaluated.expression: MUL(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), at), 0.01), 5), RANK(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(xrd, sale), 3), 2)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Dependence is a matter of frequency, not size: a research-intensive firm that has returned to the capital markets for net new money in most of the last five years has no self-sustaining funding model, and that repeated-access habit — independent of how large any single raise was — is what exposes shareholders to funding withdrawal and to serial dilution.

evaluated.name: Outside-Funded Research While Sliding Down the Industry
evaluated.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), MA(xrd, 3)), 5), RANK(NEG(SUB(IND_RANK(RATIO(xrd, sale)), LAG(IND_RANK(RATIO(xrd, sale)), 2)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: A firm whose research is paid for out of outside money while its research intensity slides down the industry ranking over a two-year span is funding a losing competitive position; the funding leg should be measured per research dollar, because the same absolute raise means something very different for a firm spending heavily on research than for one that barely researches at all.

evaluated.name: Near-Term Debt Maturities Against the Research Budget
evaluated.hypothesis: Debt coming due within the year is a hard, dated claim on internal cash; when that claim is large relative to the firm's entire research budget, research is the flexible margin that gets cut, so knowledge capital is quietly disinvested well before any earnings deterioration is visible.

Scaling the maturity wall by the research budget rather than by assets keeps the measure cross-theme and targeted at the crowding-out mechanism, and industry ranking absorbs sector differences in both normal leverage and normal research intensity.

evaluated.name: Issuance by Firms Buying Innovation Instead of Building It
evaluated.hypothesis: Within research-active firms, the mix between acquired and self-generated innovation is informative: a firm adding far more goodwill than it spends on its own research is purchasing other people's ideas at negotiated premia, and equity raised to support that strategy is the most overvaluation-prone financing of all.
evaluated.reasoning: Gen-2's goodwill test failed in portfolios because the COALESCE weight created a huge tied mass across the whole market; here goodwill additions are normalized by the firm's own research budget inside the R&D-reporter universe that every surviving signal lives in, which makes the weight continuous and the comparison a genuine build-versus-buy composition rather than a goodwill-intensity level. It is the only conditioner in the archive that measures the *source* of innovation rather than its level, trend, or competitive rank.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Research Decay Priced Only Within Issuers
evaluated.hypothesis: If the interaction is real, then among firms that actually raised meaningful equity the degree of research-franchise decay should itself sort returns; the financing event opens the door, and the intangible state determines who walks through it.
evaluated.reasoning: The critic's standing challenge to this whole family is that the base leg is the known net-issuance anomaly and the conditioner merely modulates its magnitude; replacing the continuous financing leg with a pure participation gate removes the issuance magnitude entirely, so any spread must come from the intangible conditioner within the issuer subsample. Centering the conditioner means non-issuers sit at a neutral zero in the middle while both extreme legs are populated exclusively by issuers, which is the configuration that has sorted cleanly in this archive and makes the test decisive rather than confirmatory.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Issuance by Firms With an Erratic Research Commitment
evaluated.hypothesis: A stable research budget reflects a managed portfolio of projects with credible internal funding, whereas a research budget that lurches up and down reveals opportunistic, funding-driven spending; equity raised by such firms is financing an unstable program that is likely to be abandoned.
evaluated.reasoning: Gen-1 tested the second moment of the *financing* series and found nothing (t -0.98), but the second moment of the *research* series is a different economic object — project-portfolio instability rather than funding lumpiness — and it has never been tried in this archive. It uses the validated architecture with a continuous, tie-free weight, and it discriminates a distinct pathology from Signals 1-2: erratic commitment versus measured decline.

evaluated.name: Issuance While Research Has Retreated From Its Own Peak
evaluated.hypothesis: A firm whose absolute research spending sits far below its own five-year peak has retreated from innovation; equity raised in that state cannot plausibly be funding the research program, so the proceeds are either plugging a hole or being sold on a story the firm has already stopped investing in.

considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Rescue Equity at a Retreating Research Firm
considered.hypothesis: Equity issued in the same year that long-term debt is repaid is creditor-driven balance-sheet repair rather than project funding, and it is most damaging at a firm that has simultaneously cut research below its own historical peak — the money is going to lenders while the innovation program is being abandoned.
considered.reasoning: Gen-6 showed the rescue-financing configuration produces a solid alpha (-2.4%, t -2.68) but a weak FMB slope (-1.45), and the diagnosis is its crude conditioner — a static R&D-intensity level that mostly sorts on industry — so replacing it with the retreat-from-peak state should sharpen the cross-sectional slope while preserving the alpha. The configuration itself remains invisible to every net-flow signal in the archive, since issuance and repayment cancel in net external finance.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Issuance by Firms Whose Intangible Base Was Purchased
considered.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), at), 2), RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), TS_SUM(xrd, 5)))))
considered.hypothesis: The share of a firm's intangible base that was bought rather than built is a standing measure of its innovation strategy; firms whose knowledge assets are mostly purchased goodwill have repeatedly paid acquisition premia instead of generating ideas, and equity raised to continue that strategy should be the most overvaluation-prone.
considered.reasoning: The archive's best single signal is the build-versus-buy *flow* (alpha -2.5%, t -2.72, Sharpe -0.50), whose acknowledged weakness is a large tied mass at zero for firms with no goodwill activity in a given year; expressing composition as a stock share in [0,1] gives every firm a distinct position, eliminates the event-timing noise, and should stabilize portfolio membership. It also converts an event conditioner into a persistent strategy characteristic, which lowers turnover and tests whether the effect is about deal timing or about a durable acquisitive innovation model.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Shareholder Cash In Minus Research Dollars Added
considered.hypothesis: The single number that separates the task's two poles is the net dollar flow between shareholders and the research program: money taken in from shareholders beyond what was added to research is opportunistic financing, while research expansion funded without taking shareholder money is productive intangible investment.
considered.reasoning: This is one continuous measure with an economically meaningful zero, not a rank-sum of two archived signals, and it differs from the gen-0 surplus construction by comparing financing against the *increment* to research rather than its level, which is the correct marginal comparison and removes the mechanical tilt toward research-intensive firms that the level version carried. Both tails are economically named — issuers who did not expand research at one end, self-funded research expanders at the other — so no leg is a residual pool.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Proceeds Verified as Deployed Into Research
considered.hypothesis: Among firms that raised meaningful equity last year, the ones that visibly expanded the research budget this year used the proceeds as advertised, while those whose research budget did not move raised money for reasons the market was not told; the subsequent return difference is the price of that verification.
considered.reasoning: This is a lead-lag audit of the use of proceeds rather than the archive's contemporaneous self-funding test, so it is not the failed Self-Funded-Research-Expansion mechanism in continuous form: the population here consists entirely of *issuers*, and the question is what happened to the money afterwards. Non-issuers sit at a neutral zero while both extreme legs are prior-year issuers, giving the cleanest possible test of whether the market distinguishes productive from opportunistic intangible financing after the fact.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Research Financed by Non-Debt Liabilities
considered.hypothesis: Firms can fund a research program without touching capital markets by stretching payables and other non-debt obligations; a large increase in non-debt liabilities relative to the research budget means the innovation program is being carried by counterparties, which is a fragile funding source that reverses when suppliers tighten.
considered.reasoning: Total liabilities net of interest-bearing debt is a financing channel this archive has never used, and expressing its change per research dollar keeps the measure genuinely cross-theme while leaving the well-worn issuance and repurchase variables out of the expression entirely. It sits in the ratio family that produced the archive's strongest cross-sectional slopes, with an always-positive denominator among R&D reporters and industry ranking to absorb sector differences in working-capital norms.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Three-Year Raise With No Research Deployment
considered.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(SUB(sstk, prstkc), 3), at), 2), RANK(NEG(SUB(RATIO(xrd, at), LAG(RATIO(xrd, at), 3)))))
considered.hypothesis: A firm that has raised equity repeatedly over three years while its research intensity is no higher than it was three years ago never deployed the money into the innovation program it was raising against; the promised investment simply did not happen.
considered.reasoning: The conditioner is not a contemporaneous state variable like every accepted conditioner in the archive but a matched-horizon audit — the change in research intensity measured over exactly the window in which the money was raised — which makes the interaction a deployment failure rather than a franchise-quality amplifier, and it is not entangled with the financing leg the way the book-equity conditioner was. Paired with Signal 2 it brackets the deployment mechanism from both poles, so the two together identify whether verified use of proceeds is what the market misprices.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Rescue Equity at an Acquisition-Built Firm
considered.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(MIN(sstk, dltr), at), 2), RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), TS_SUM(xrd, 5)))))
considered.hypothesis: Equity raised to repay debt is most damaging at a firm whose intangible base was purchased rather than built, because the leverage being repaid was originally incurred to buy other people's ideas and the collateral behind it cannot be liquidated without destroying the business.
considered.reasoning: Rescue-equity financing produced the archive's largest alpha (-3.3%, t -3.28) but its weakest cross-sectional slope (-1.40), and the diagnosis is its conditioner — a static R&D-to-sales level that mostly sorts industries — whereas the purchased-intangible-share conditioner is a bounded, persistent firm characteristic that independently produced FMB -2.77 with alpha -2.0%. Pairing the strongest configuration with the conditioner that carries cross-sectional power directly targets the one metric where the best portfolio signal is deficient.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Issuance Amid Purchased-Intangible Churn
considered.hypothesis: Large movement in purchased intangibles in either direction — big acquisitions or big write-offs — relative to the firm's own research budget marks a deal-driven rather than organic innovation strategy; equity raised by such firms funds a serial dealmaking process whose track record already includes reversals.
considered.reasoning: The archive tested goodwill *additions* (alpha -2.5%) but never the magnitude of goodwill movement, and using ABS turns a directional flow into an activity measure so that impairment years — the revelation of failed prior deals — enter the short leg alongside acquisition years instead of being pushed to the long leg where they economically do not belong. Scaling by the firm's own research budget keeps the comparison a strategy-composition measure inside the R&D-reporter universe where portfolio alpha has consistently survived.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Share of the Research Budget Covered by Outside Money
considered.hypothesis: The economically bounded question is what fraction of this year's research program could have been paid for out of money raised from outside investors; a program essentially fully covered by external funds is a program that continues only while capital markets stay open, whereas one covered marginally is substantially self-financed.
considered.reasoning: Capping the external inflow at the size of the research budget converts the archive's unbounded funding-per-research multiple — whose extreme deciles are dominated by a handful of enormous raises — into a coverage share in roughly the unit interval, which is exactly the outlier problem behind that signal's strong FMB slope but modest alpha. Using gross inflows rather than net flows also means the measure does not cancel against repayments, so it is a different object from the archived net-external-finance ratio rather than a dividend-for-debt substitution into an existing template.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Debt Retired While Research Expands
considered.hypothesis: A firm paying down lenders in the same year it adds dollars to its research budget is generating enough internal cash to satisfy creditors and expand innovation simultaneously; that joint act, made to the creditor rather than the shareholder, is a hard signal of a self-financing intangible franchise.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the churn construction — whose selection on large cash-rich repurchasers indeed fought its stated negative sign — with the creditor-side counterpart of the archive's only working long pole, which asks whether the productive-pole result is about surplus cash generation in general or specifically about equity-market signalling through buybacks. Both arguments are non-negative, identically asset-scaled dollar flows, and the bottom leg is firms cutting research in dollars, so both extremes remain economically identified.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Issuance as Total Soft-Capital Spending Retreats
considered.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), at), 2), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), TS_MAX(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 5)))))
considered.hypothesis: Intangible investment is not only research: for consumer and services firms the brand budget plays the identical role, so the informative state is retreat from the firm's own peak in total soft-capital spending, research plus advertising, and equity raised during such a retreat funds a franchise the firm has itself stopped supporting.
considered.reasoning: Advertising is the one intangible variable in the resource menu this archive has never used, and treating an unreported line as zero spending is the economically correct convention when the other line is reported, so the conditioner extends the retreat mechanism to brand-driven firms and should widen the R&D-reporter universe that has constrained every result to about 5% coverage. It is a change in the definition of intangible capital rather than a re-scaling of an existing measure, and it directly tests whether the mechanism is about research specifically or about soft capital generally.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cash Returned With Research and Margin Both Building
considered.expression: WINSOR(MIN(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, sstk), at), MIN(RATIO(DELTA(xrd, 1), at), RATIO(DELTA(SUB(sale, cogs), 1), at))), 2)
considered.hypothesis: The fully productive state requires three things at once: cash genuinely returned to shareholders on a net basis, a research budget being expanded, and gross profit rising to validate that the intangible investment is working; a firm satisfying all three is self-financing an innovation program whose output is already visible.
considered.reasoning: Rather than lengthening the horizon of the archived long-pole signal — a parameter change that would mostly load on size and growth persistence — this adds an independent output-verification leg, gross profit growth, so that research expansions unaccompanied by any realized margin improvement no longer qualify. The nested MIN keeps all three arguments as identically asset-scaled dollar flows, and netting issuance out of the repurchase leg removes firms whose buybacks merely offset option-related issuance, which was the main contamination in the one-year version.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Net Cash Returned With Research Expanding
considered.hypothesis: The productive pole is a firm that is a genuine net returner of cash — not one whose buybacks merely offset option issuance — while simultaneously adding dollars to its research budget, since only that combination demonstrates surplus cash generation alongside continued innovation investment.
considered.reasoning: The archive brackets this precisely: the gross-buyback version delivered the alpha (+2.2%, t +2.06) but a weak slope, while the triple conjunction with a margin leg delivered a strong slope (+2.85) but no alpha, indicating that netting issuance out of the payout leg is the useful part and the third leg over-restricts the sample. This two-leg net version is the untested interpolation between two evaluated points and is the archive's best remaining chance at a long pole with joint support.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Years of Research Bought With Paper
considered.hypothesis: The dollar amount of stock-financed goodwill, expressed as a multiple of the firm's annual research budget, states how many years of internal innovation the firm chose to buy instead of build with the paper it issued.
considered.reasoning: This states the archive's most reliable conditioning mechanism as a single ratio rather than a product, using the research-budget denominator that has produced the strongest cross-sectional slopes (-3.75 to -4.32) while keeping the acquisitive economics that produce the strongest portfolio alphas, and MIN ensures only the jointly funded and jointly capitalized amount counts. Industry ranking after winsorization bounds the measure so its extreme deciles are homogeneous in funding-versus-research terms, addressing the exact defect that left earlier unbounded gap measures with strong slopes but unreliable alphas.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Diverted Dollars Net of Research Added Per Research Year
considered.hypothesis: The decisive quantity is the balance between dollars raised that were absorbed by creditors and dealmaking and dollars actually added to the research budget, expressed in units of the firm's own annual research spending so that the comparison is meaningful for a biotech and a diversified manufacturer alike.
considered.reasoning: Capping the diversion at gross equity issued keeps the first term non-negative, so the lower tail is no longer mechanical net repurchases — it is now firms adding research dollars without any diverted raise, which is genuinely intangible content at both poles and answers the critic's objection directly. Industry ranking of a research-scaled measure is the construction that has produced this archive's strongest cross-sectional slopes, while the subtraction of the research increment keeps the economics of use-of-proceeds rather than of financing volume.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Diverted Dollars Net of Research Added Per Asset
considered.hypothesis: The same use-of-proceeds balance — money absorbed by creditors and deals minus money added to research — should also be informative when scaled by firm size rather than by the research budget, since asset scaling preserves the economic magnitude of large raises that research scaling compresses.
considered.reasoning: This archive has repeatedly shown that scaling choice, not economic content, determines which metric a signal wins on — asset-scaled dollar measures deliver portfolio alpha while bounded research-scaled ratios deliver cross-sectional slopes — so pairing this with Signal 1 isolates that single design dimension on an identical new measure and tells us which side of the trade-off the diverted-proceeds mechanism sits on. There is no rank multiplier here, so neither tail is amplified and the long leg remains firms expanding research without a diverted raise.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Issuance While Purchased Technology Amortizes Away
considered.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), at), 2), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(intan, 1), DELTA(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), 1)), MA(xrd, 3)), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: Separating the intangible balance into goodwill and identifiable intangibles reveals whether purchased technology, patents and customer relationships are being replenished or simply amortized away; a firm whose identifiable intangibles are eroding relative to its research budget is losing acquired capability, and equity raised in that state funds a shrinking asset base.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the cosmetic blend of two goodwill measures with a decomposition of the intangible balance sheet that the archive has never used — the change in intangibles net of the change in goodwill isolates identifiable intangible assets, whose amortization is economically distinct from goodwill activity and from research spending. The conditioner is continuous, research-scaled and free of the tied mass that the goodwill-flow weights carry for firms with no deal activity.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Diversion of Proceeds Priced Within Issuers
considered.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), at), 0.02), ZSCORE(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(dltr, ABS(DELTA(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), 1))), MA(xrd, 3)), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: Among firms that actually raised meaningful equity, those whose debt repayments and purchased-intangible transactions are large relative to their research budget used the proceeds for everything except research, and that distinction — not the size of the raise — should sort returns within the issuer population.
considered.reasoning: Replacing the dividend channel, which is empty for most R&D reporters, with the two non-research uses that actually have mass in this universe puts real economic content behind the "proceeds went elsewhere" claim, and gating on issuance removes the tail-amplification problem entirely because the financing leg no longer carries a sign. The gen-5 within-issuer test showed that franchise *decay* prices nothing once issuance magnitude is removed; this asks the same decisive question of use-of-proceeds, which is the one conditioning dimension that produced the archive's largest alphas.
considered.author: proposer

critic_notes.target_name: Internally Funded Innovation Intensity
critic_notes.rationale: This is a simple additive blend of two separately well-documented anomalies (R&D intensity and net external financing) with no genuine conditioning, so a positive result would be almost entirely attributable to the known components rather than to any cross-theme interaction.

critic_notes.target_name: Equity-Financed Intangible Expansion
critic_notes.rationale: The construction is internally consistent and the sign is right, though it sits close to the known stock-financed-acquisition underperformance result, and the claim that the rank product "fires only when both conditions hold" overstates what a monotone product of ranks actually does.

critic_notes.target_name: Debt-Financed Acquired Intangibles
critic_notes.rationale: The debt-plus-goodwill fragility mechanism is coherent and the sign matches the expression, but COALESCE(gdwl, intan) silently mixes two economically different quantities across firms (goodwill additions vs. total intangible changes), which contaminates cross-sectional comparability and partly overlaps the asset-growth anomaly.

critic_notes.target_name: Dilution-Adjusted Knowledge Capital
critic_notes.rationale: This is a near-duplicate of "Internally Funded Innovation Intensity" in a different wrapper and amounts to the R&D-intensity anomaly plus the composite-share-issuance anomaly (Pontiff-Woodgate) added together, i.e., a rediscovery of two published effects rather than a new interaction.

critic_notes.target_name: External Finance per Unit of Intangible Capital
critic_notes.rationale: With intan+xrd near zero for a large share of firms and a numerator that changes sign, the cross-sectional dispersion will be driven by the inverse of intangible intensity and by denominator blowups (1% winsorization is far too mild), so the signal is a noisy re-scaling of the known net-external-financing anomaly.

critic_notes.target_name: Productivity-Signed Intangible Financing
critic_notes.rationale: This is a genuinely conditional, sign-flipping interaction whose hypothesis, expression, and expected sign are mutually consistent; the main risks are that SIGN discards trend magnitude and that revt/MA(xrd,3) restricts coverage to R&D reporters, both of which are testable rather than disqualifying.

critic_notes.target_name: Equity-Funded Innovation Premium
critic_notes.rationale: This is essentially the archived Payout-Signed R&D Intensity with the switch made continuous and the expected sign reversed post hoc, and because both legs are demeaned the product is equally large for low-R&D/low-issuance firms, so the "premium to equity-funded R&D" story does not match what the expression actually ranks (and the positive sign fights the well-documented net-equity-issuance anomaly).

critic_notes.target_name: Debt-Funded Innovation Discount
critic_notes.rationale: The debt-overhang-on-soft-assets mechanism applied to organic R&D is a defensible and reasonably distinct test from the gen-0 acquired-intangible version, though the double-demeaned product means the long leg also loads on low-R&D/low-debt-issuance firms, muddying the conditional interpretation.

critic_notes.target_name: Levered Soft-Asset Balance Sheet
critic_notes.rationale: A coherent stock-level asset-composition/capital-structure mismatch with a genuine coverage advantage over the gen-0 flow signals, but it is close to a mechanical product of two heavily studied characteristics (intangible intensity and leverage) and inherits the same four-quadrant sign ambiguity from centering both legs.

critic_notes.target_name: Stock-Financed Intangible Conjunction
critic_notes.rationale: MIN is not the logical AND claimed: because DELTA(intan) is frequently negative while sstk/at is bounded below at zero, the signal collapses to intangible shrinkage/impairment for a large share of firms, so the bottom leg captures intangible write-downs rather than "no stock-financed expansion," and the two ratios have non-comparable scales.

critic_notes.target_name: Innovation Under Unstable External Funding
critic_notes.rationale: Conditioning intangible intensity on the second moment of financing flows is a genuinely new angle in this archive, but the 5-year VOL on annual data will be noisy and coverage-thin, and the centered product again implies an unintended prediction for low-R&D/stable-financing firms.

critic_notes.target_name: Dilution Amplified by Intangible Opacity
critic_notes.rationale: A monotone [0,1] amplifier on share-issuance growth is largely a rediscovery of the well-known net share issuance anomaly rather than an identified interaction, and raw csho growth is contaminated by stock splits, which will dominate the extreme leg.

critic_notes.target_name: Serial Issuance Against a Research Peak
critic_notes.rationale: This is essentially the archived "Proceeds-Into-Research Issuance" with the issuance horizon stretched from one to three years and the expected sign silently flipped to match that signal's realized (contrary-to-hypothesis) outcome — a post-hoc sign reversal on a near-duplicate construction, and multi-year net issuance is itself the well-documented composite-issuance anomaly.

critic_notes.target_name: Issuance Into Decaying Research Productivity
critic_notes.rationale: A defensible repair of the gen-0 SIGN-based productivity signal — the bounded non-negative rank weight is internally consistent with the negative expected sign and preserves trend information the SIGN operator discarded — though the mechanism remains an issuance anomaly with a conditioning variable and coverage will stay near 4% among R&D reporters with three-year trends.

critic_notes.target_name: Buybacks Backed by Intangible Profitability
critic_notes.rationale: This is the arithmetic product of two separately published anomalies (Novy-Marx gross profitability and net share issuance/repurchase), so the spread will be dominated by their main effects rather than any interaction, and gross-margin-on-assets is a weak stand-in for "intangible franchise" — the intangible theme is essentially absent from the expression.

critic_notes.target_name: Issuance by Goodwill-Built Firms
critic_notes.rationale: Cleanly separates acquired from organic intangible capital as the conditioning variable, is internally consistent (signed issuance times a non-negative goodwill-intensity weight, negative sign), and improves coverage, though the COALESCE-to-zero convention creates a large tied mass at the bottom rank and the construction sits close to both the goodwill/acquisition and share-issuance literatures.

critic_notes.target_name: Industry-Neutral Financing Surplus Over Intangible Needs
critic_notes.rationale: The industry-contamination diagnosis is economically reasonable, but the edit is the archived gen-0 signal with a standard z-score swapped for an industry z-score and the intangible gate dropped — a normalization tweak rather than a substantively different mechanism, and removing the gate also removes the only conditional/cross-theme element.

critic_notes.target_name: Intangible Contraction After the Raise
critic_notes.rationale: The lead-lag structure (accumulated past issuance interacted with current intangible contraction) is genuinely distinct from the archive's contemporaneous pairings and the sign is coherent, but because both factors are non-negative the signal has a large degenerate mass at zero, so the long leg is an undifferentiated pool of non-issuers and the portfolio sort may be unstable.

critic_notes.target_name: Total External Finance Into Decaying Research Productivity
critic_notes.rationale: This is a cosmetic instrument-swap on the archive's gen-2 "Issuance Into Decaying Research Productivity" (equity → equity+debt) and simultaneously re-treads gen-0's "Productivity-Signed Intangible Financing," which already paired the identical total-net-external-finance flow with a sale/R&D trend conditioner, so it adds a design-choice ablation rather than a new economic mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Cash Distribution From a Knowledge Franchise
critic_notes.rationale: This is essentially the archive's "Dividend Commitment at Knowledge-Intensive Firms" with repurchases appended and the expected sign flipped to match that signal's realized (negative) outcome — sign-fitting to a prior result is not an ex-ante hypothesis, and net payout yield conditioned on R&D is close enough to the known payout/net-external-financing anomalies to be a rediscovery.

critic_notes.target_name: Payout Accelerating as Research Decelerates
critic_notes.rationale: The change-on-change construction is a genuinely distinct event-based test from the archive's level-based payout×R&D signals and the payout-versus-research reallocation channel is separate from the financing-versus-intangible-investment version already tried, though the conditioner DELTA(xrd/sale) is contaminated by sales growth (falling R&D intensity from a sales surge is good news, not harvesting), which will blur the sort.

critic_notes.target_name: Deleveraging on an Improving Research Engine
critic_notes.rationale: Because the [0,1] rank conditioner only modulates magnitude and never flips sign, the signal is dominated by net debt retirement scaled by assets — a direct restatement of the well-documented net-debt-issuance/external-financing anomaly — and its double sign-flip relative to the archive's best result makes it a mechanical mirror rather than an independent identification of the "good pole."

critic_notes.target_name: Debt-Tilted Financing Mix for Soft-Asset Firms
critic_notes.rationale: The expression's two legs fight each other: subtracting net equity issuance assigns high signal values to firms that are *repurchasing* equity, which the archive repeatedly shows predicts high returns, so the stated negative sign requires the debt-overhang effect to dominate a component whose known direction is opposite — an internal tension the proposal does not address, on top of substantial overlap with gen-1's inconclusive "Debt-Funded Innovation Discount."

critic_notes.target_name: Issuance While Losing the Innovation Race
critic_notes.rationale: Relative within-industry R&D position and its one-year change is a genuinely new conditioning variable in this archive, it nets out sector-wide research and technology-cost cycles that contaminate own-firm sale-per-R&D trends, and the bounded continuous weight avoids the tied-mass degeneracies that broke earlier sorts — though the base leg remains the familiar net equity issuance anomaly, so the burden is on the conditioner to add incremental information.

critic_notes.target_name: Chronic External Dependence of the Research Program
critic_notes.rationale: This is a horizon re-parameterization of the archive's "External Funding Intensity of the Research Program" (same numerator variables, same denominator concept, only 3-year sums replacing the 1-year/3-year-MA pairing), which is precisely the kind of cosmetic variant that adds smoothing rather than a new economic distinction, and the "chronic vs. one-off" claim is not actually identified because a single large raise in the window still dominates the three-year sum.

critic_notes.target_name: Externally Funded While Losing the Innovation Race
critic_notes.rationale: The economic motivation for complementarity is fair, but the stated construction is internally inconsistent — ZSCORE of an IND_RANK centers the funding leg at the *industry median* of the ratio, not at zero net financing, so the claimed "net payers score negative" sign-flip point is wrong and the multiplicative weight will flip sign for firms that are still net raisers; combined with an intersected sub-5% universe and near-duplication of the archive's existing "Issuance While Losing the Innovation Race," the incremental information is likely small.

critic_notes.target_name: Allocation Shift From Research to Shareholders
critic_notes.rationale: The diagnosis (level ratio's large alpha with wrong-signed FMB slope is a maturity/factor-loading sort) is correct and within-firm demeaning is the right decisive test, though the archive's already-failed "Payout Accelerating as Research Decelerates" tests essentially the same change-based harvesting event and suggests the answer will be a null, and the MA-of-a-ratio-of-a-ratio construction is numerically fragile even after winsorization.

critic_notes.target_name: Debt Service Crowding Out Research
critic_notes.rationale: The claim that gross repayment is "mechanically unrelated to net financing" is false — dltr enters the archive's strongest signal with a negative sign, so this proposal predicts *low* returns for exactly the firms that signal marks as high-return, an unacknowledged sign contradiction; on top of that, dltr/R&D is dominated by leverage scale and debt-maturity structure rather than any crowding-out of the research budget.

critic_notes.target_name: Issuance as Pricing Power Erodes
critic_notes.rationale: A legitimate external-validity test that escapes the R&D-reporter universe with a defensible alternative intangible-output proxy and a clean nonnegative weight, but it risks largely reloading on the well-known net share issuance anomaly conditioned by the equally well-known gross-margin-change signal, so the burden is on showing the interaction beats the additive combination of its two published parts.

critic_notes.target_name: New Claims Per Dollar of Total Intangible Capital
critic_notes.rationale: Changing the scaler from a flow to an intangible capital stock is a substantive rather than cosmetic revision and the coverage expansion to non-R&D intangible-heavy firms is a real test of mechanism generality, but for firms with small intan and zero-coalesced R&D the denominator can be near-zero, so the extreme deciles may be scaler noise rather than dilution — report results with and without a minimum-denominator screen.

critic_notes.target_name: Issuance Into a Doubly Confirmed Research Decline
critic_notes.rationale: This is a mechanical rank-average of the two best already-tested conditioners bolted onto the identical net-issuance leg, so it adds no new economic content and its outcome is largely predictable as a blend of the two parent signals (both ~-2% alpha, t≈-2.5) rather than a test of a new mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Issuance Against Lagged Research Payoff Decay
critic_notes.rationale: The lag has a defensible innovation-timing rationale, but it is a single-operator edit of the gen-2 signal that will push coverage below its already thin 0.042 (a 3-year trend of a 3-year MA lagged 2 years needs ~8 years of xrd history), and the conditioner remains dominated by the sales trend rather than by research productivity per se.

critic_notes.target_name: Issuance by Firms Buying Innovation Instead of Building It
critic_notes.rationale: Build-versus-buy composition scaled by the firm's own research budget is a genuinely different conditioner from the archive's goodwill-level and intangible-growth tests, though it overlaps conceptually with the gen-0 equity-financed-intangible-expansion and gen-2 goodwill signals and still carries a large tied mass at zero for R&D firms with no goodwill activity.

critic_notes.target_name: Issuance Against an Unmonetized Knowledge Stock
critic_notes.rationale: The conditioner is essentially the classic R&D-intensity (Lev–Sougiannis / Chan–Lakonishok–Sougiannis) anomaly with the sign reversed, and it directly contradicts the archive's strongest ratio result (financing per dollar of accumulated intangible capital, t=-4.3), which implies issuance is worst when the knowledge stock is *small*, a conflict the proposal never addresses.

critic_notes.target_name: Research Decay Priced Only Within Issuers
critic_notes.rationale: Replacing the continuous issuance leg with a participation gate is the correct decisive test of whether the intangible conditioner prices anything independent of the known net-issuance anomaly, and the centered conditioner keeps both extreme legs populated by issuers; the main risk is that the large zero mass of non-issuers bleeds into the extreme quintiles and dilutes the portfolio spread.

critic_notes.target_name: Issuance by Firms With an Erratic Research Commitment
critic_notes.rationale: Second-moment instability of the research program is a distinct economic object from the gen-1 financing-volatility test and is untried here, but VOL(xrd/sale) is strongly confounded with firm size, age and idiosyncratic volatility, so any result will need a check that it is not a repackaged vol/size effect.

critic_notes.target_name: Three-Year Stock-Financed Acquisition of Innovation
critic_notes.rationale: This is a horizon rescaling of the gen-5 "Issuance by Firms Buying Innovation Instead of Building It" signal (same two legs, same conditioning logic, only 1-year windows swapped for 3-year sums), i.e. a parameter tweak rather than a substantively different mechanism, and the three-year issuance leg also drifts toward the well-documented composite share-issuance anomaly.

critic_notes.target_name: Proceeds Grew the Balance Sheet, Not the Research
critic_notes.rationale: Use-of-proceeds (asset growth outrunning R&D growth) is a genuinely new conditioning dimension in this archive and is internally consistent with the negative sign, but the conditioner is largely the asset-growth/investment anomaly interacted with the issuance anomaly — two known effects multiplied — and GROWTH(xrd,1) is very noisy for small or newly reported R&D, so any result will need to be shown incremental to CMA and to plain asset growth.

critic_notes.target_name: Issuance by Firms Both Retreating From and Erratic in Research
critic_notes.rationale: The two conditioners being conjoined were already tested separately and produced nearly identical statistics (alpha -0.023/-0.020, t -2.54/-2.23, Sharpe -0.48/-0.47), which strongly suggests both are near-passive multipliers on a common issuance leg, so their product is an incremental recombination of evaluated material rather than an independent test, and it will mostly shrink effective breadth.

critic_notes.target_name: Issuing More Than Industry Peers While Research Retreats
critic_notes.rationale: Peer-benchmarking the financing leg is a defensible idea, but as constructed this is a one-operator normalization variant of the already-evaluated "Issuance While Research Has Retreated From Its Own Peak," and IND_ZSCORE destroys the economically meaningful zero point so that below-average issuers (including net repurchasers) in high-issuance industries receive negative scores and are placed in the long leg — a change the hypothesis never addresses.

critic_notes.target_name: Cash Returned by an Improving Innovator
critic_notes.rationale: Algebraically this equals the gen-2 "Issuance Into Decaying Research Productivity" signal minus the raw net-issuance term (since RANK(NEG(x)) ≈ 1 − RANK(x)), so it is heavily collinear with already-evaluated content, and because the residual issuance term itself carries a negative slope the stated positive expected sign is not actually implied by the construction.

critic_notes.target_name: Issuance by Firms With a Short Research Track Record
critic_notes.rationale: Reporting persistence is a conditioner dimension not yet tested and is a useful diagnostic on whether the family is driven by intermittent R&D reporters, but the leg is coarsely discrete (0–5 with heavy ties), likely proxies for firm age and size rather than credibility per se, and the claimed coverage gain is doubtful since TS_COUNT still requires a usable xrd history.

critic_notes.target_name: Two-Pole Innovation Financing Spread
critic_notes.rationale: This is a mechanical rank-sum of two already-evaluated archive signals with no new economic content, and the weaker leg (buybacks-alongside-research, fmb 1.68, Sharpe 0.005) is likely to dilute rather than extend the spread, so it functions as metric-blending rather than a substantive refinement.

critic_notes.target_name: Net Cash Returned While Research Grows
critic_notes.rationale: The mechanism — research expansion funded internally by a net returner of capital — is essentially the archive's already-failed "Self-Funded Research Expansion" (fmb -0.50, wrong-signed alpha) with a continuous MIN replacing the indicator, making it an incremental variant of two evaluated signals rather than a new hypothesis.

critic_notes.target_name: Funding-Intensity and Research-Retreat Hybrid
critic_notes.rationale: Explicitly a SUMRANK of two previously evaluated signals chosen because one scores well on FMB and the other on alpha; this is cosmetic metric-optimization on largely overlapping issuance-based information, not a new mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Rescue Equity at a Retreating Research Firm
critic_notes.rationale: A coherent recombination in which the identified weakness (a static, largely industry-driven R&D-level conditioner) is replaced by a firm-relative research-retreat state, and the MIN(sstk, dltr) configuration remains genuinely invisible to net-flow measures — though it is still a recombination of two archived legs and risks simply re-averaging their spreads.

critic_notes.target_name: Issuance While the Equity Base Burns Away
critic_notes.rationale: The conditioner is mechanically entangled with the signal leg (net issuance is itself a component of DELTA(ceq)) and, once that is netted out, reduces to accumulated losses per research dollar — i.e. an issuance × profitability/burn interaction close to the archive's gross-margin-per-R&D version and to the well-known issuance and profitability anomalies FF5 already partly spans.

critic_notes.target_name: Issuance by Firms Whose Intangible Base Was Purchased
critic_notes.rationale: Converting the build-versus-buy conditioner from a noisy annual flow into a bounded stock share of the firm's own intangible base is a substantively motivated fix to a diagnosed tied-mass and turnover problem, and the R&D-stock denominator makes it materially different from the archive's failed gdwl/at version, though it remains within the same mechanism family.

critic_notes.target_name: Equity Raised While Dividends Are Maintained
critic_notes.rationale: This is a single-argument substitution (dltr→dvc) into the archived "Rescue Equity at a Retreating Research Firm" template with an identical conditioner, and because sstk is small for most firms (option exercises) MIN(sstk,dvc) will usually collapse to sstk within the dividend-payer subsample, making the signal largely a re-expression of the well-known equity-issuance anomaly conditioned on dividend status.

critic_notes.target_name: Issue-and-Repurchase Churn at Research Firms
critic_notes.rationale: The stated orthogonality claim is false — MIN(sstk,prstkc) is strongly correlated with the levels of both flows, not with their difference — and since the measure mechanically selects large, cash-rich repurchasers (a group associated with *positive* abnormal returns), the natural direction of the expression works against the negative expected sign.

critic_notes.target_name: Rescue Equity at an Acquisition-Built Firm
critic_notes.rationale: A defensible diagnosis-driven recombination that pairs the archive's strongest portfolio configuration with its most cross-sectionally powerful conditioner, though the reasoning misattributes the archived rescue-equity conditioner (retreat-from-peak, not static R&D/sales) and the result may simply interpolate between two already-tested signals rather than add new information.

critic_notes.target_name: Issuance Amid Purchased-Intangible Churn
critic_notes.rationale: Replacing signed goodwill change with its absolute magnitude is a substantive, well-motivated construct change (impairment years join acquisition years in the short leg rather than the long leg) rather than a cosmetic tweak, but the gain over the archived signed-goodwill version is likely modest since large positive goodwill changes dominate the right tail either way.

critic_notes.target_name: Net Shareholder Funding Per Year of Research
critic_notes.rationale: This is essentially the archived "External Funding Intensity of the Research Program" (IND_RANK of net external financing over MA(xrd,3), fmb −4.09, alpha −1.7%) with the debt legs dropped and a Δxrd term added, so it is a re-scaling recombination of two existing archive members that will be highly collinear with both rather than a new mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Cash Returned Through a Sustained Research Build
critic_notes.rationale: Changing DELTA(xrd,1) to a three-year difference in the archived "Buybacks Alongside Research Expansion" is a horizon parameter tweak, not a substantively different mechanism, and it also mechanically raises the signal's exposure to firm size and growth persistence, which risks a spurious apparent improvement in the long leg.

critic_notes.target_name: Raise Absorbed by Creditors and Dealmaking
critic_notes.rationale: The MIN cap is only binding for issuers, so the entire lower (long) tail collapses to net share repurchases scaled by assets — i.e., the published net-stock-issuance/payout anomaly with no intangible content — and the archive already contains a closely related dollar-scaled net-flow measure ("Shareholder Cash In Minus Research Dollars Added," fmb -4.25).

critic_notes.target_name: Diverted Proceeds at a Retreating Research Firm
critic_notes.rationale: This is a near-duplicate of the already-evaluated "Rescue Equity at a Retreating Research Firm" (MIN(sstk,dltr) × identical retreat conditioner, alpha -3.3%, t -3.28) with |Δgdwl| bolted on, and the product of a two-sided financing leg with a non-negative rank amplifies both tails, so the long leg becomes big repurchasers *with* retreating research — the opposite of the stated economics.

critic_notes.target_name: Issuance by Acquisitive Firms Currently Transacting
critic_notes.rationale: Both conditioners are already-evaluated goodwill measures built from the same variable with nearly identical statistics (alpha -2.0%/-2.3%, Sharpe -0.46/-0.50) attached to the identical net-issuance leg, so averaging their ranks is a cosmetic blend rather than a new mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Raise Shipped Straight Back Out to Claimholders
critic_notes.rationale: Adding dvc to dltr inside the MIN and swapping sstk for net issuance leaves this essentially the archived "Rescue Equity at a Retreating Research Firm," and because dvc is zero for most R&D-reporting firms the incremental economic content of the "dividend recipients" channel is negligible.

critic_notes.target_name: Net Cash Returned With Research Expanding
critic_notes.rationale: A single-operator change from the gen-6 signal, but the gross-versus-net payout distinction is economically meaningful and the archive's two bracketing results (alpha without slope, slope without alpha) give a genuine diagnostic reason to test the interpolation, though much of the incremental variation is the known net-issuance effect.

critic_notes.target_name: Years of Research Bought With Paper
critic_notes.rationale: Well-constructed and internally consistent — the MIN isolates the jointly issued-and-capitalized dollar amount, the R&D-budget denominator is the scaling that produced the archive's strongest slopes, and winsorization plus IND_RANK controls the small-denominator blow-up — with the caveat that stock-financed-acquirer underperformance is itself a documented result, so the novelty rests on the R&D scaling.
